facts.fact: 三个字：他消失了整整三天，她一条消息都没等到。
facts.anchor: But it’s been three days since I’ve heard from him.

facts.fact: 她的猜测：他大概早把「你是唯一能碰到我的人」这句老话讲过无数遍。
facts.anchor: He’s probably used the old you’re the only person who’s able to touch me line a million times.

facts.fact: Jess 正在做婚礼前的最后一次试衣，Lucy 在店里的候客区等她出来亮相。
facts.anchor: Jess is having her final dress fitting right now, and I’m waiting in the lobby for her to come out and show me how gorgeous she is.

facts.fact: 她从椅子旁的篮子里随手抽了一本婚礼杂志，一直翻到一篇讲平价蜜月目的地的文章。
facts.anchor: I pick up a wedding magazine at random from the basket next to my chair and flip through it until I land on an article about affordable honeymoon destinations.

facts.fact: 她读杂志里写 Sedona, Arizona 的水晶段落，读得有好几分钟完全不去想 Daniel。
facts.anchor: I’m so absorbed in reading about Sedona, Arizona—they’re really into crystals there, apparently; who knew?—that I manage to stop thinking about Daniel for several entire minutes.

facts.fact: 他毫无预兆地现身，她惊叫出声，差点把手里的《Bride Monthly》四月号掉了。
facts.anchor: “Shit!” I shout, so startled that I almost drop the April issue of Bride Monthly.

facts.fact: 店后面出声的是 Ms. Devon——经营这家店的年长裁缝。
facts.anchor: “Lucy?” Ms. Devon, the elderly seamstress who owns this shop, calls out from the back.

facts.fact: 试完礼服后去 Heartwarming Café 是 r/TennesseeBride 上给田纳西准新娘的推荐节目。
facts.anchor: Visiting the Heartwarming Café after having your dress fitting is, according to r/TennesseeBride, the thing to do if you’re a Middle Tennessee bride-to-be.
